data.name: Aighar
data.gender_notes: Aighar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'Aghr', meaning 'to rise', 'to be exalted'. In Islamic context, Aighar symbolizes the virtues of nobility, excellence, and exaltedness. The name Aighar carries the meaning “Exalted, Noble” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aighar usually hope their child will grow to embody exalted, noble and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name of noble character and divine favor.
data.etymology: Aighar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Exalted, Noble.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aighar total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

He was born in the city of Maragheh and studied under the renowned poet and scholar Omar Khayyam. Aighar's poetry reflects the cultural and intellectual richness of the Seljuk Empire in Persia during the Middle Ages.

Aighar al-Masihi, also known as Abd al-Rahman ibn Yahya, was a 9th-century Andalusian scholar and philosopher. He was born in Cordoba and studied under the great scholar Al-Kindi. Aighar is notable for his work in logic, metaphysics, and theology, which drew from both Islamic and Greek philosophical traditions. His writings were influential in the development of Islamic scholasticism in Spain during the Middle Ages.
